provision_review.why: HB 136 §1-1 rewrites 48-7-29.10(a) to set the credit at 50 percent of the federal Section 21 credit, and §3-1(b) applies that change to taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025. The pre-fix module keeps 0.30 open-ended from 2008, so it returns 30% for 2025 and later. provision.txt, the codified section, still reads 'Thirty percent for all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2008', which supports the pre-fix rule.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The 30% rate version carried effective_from 2008-01-01 with no effective_to, so the module returned 0.30 of the federal Section 21 credit for 2025 and later even though HB 136 (2025) amended 48-7-29.10(a) to 50 percent, applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025.
triage.triage_notes: Read HB 136 through the pinned corpus: Section 1-1 rewrites 48-7-29.10(a) to 'The amount of such credit shall be equal to 50 percent of the amount of the credit provided for in Section 21 of the Internal Revenue Code', and Section 3-1(b) states 'Section 1-1 of this Act shall be applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025.' The fix bounds versions[2] at '2024-12-31' and adds versions[3] 0.50 from 2025-01-01 with two proof atoms quoting exactly those sentences, plus the module citation-paths list gains the act. Nothing else in the module changed (the credit formula, carryforward and prior-year branches are untouched). Alternative kind: amount_mismatch (0.30 vs 0.50 for 2025+); I chose wrong_period_or_effective_date for the same reason as index 0. Follow-up commit 5474dca0e adds an effective_to proof atom and narrows the rule's source string from '(a)(1)-(3)' to '(a)'.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module encoded the 30% rate version with effective_from 2008-01-01 and no effective_to, so it returned 0.30 of the federal Section 21 credit for 2025 and later; the fix bounds that version at 2024-12-31 and adds a 2025-01-01 version at 0.50, i.e. it changes an existing output value for 2025+ rather than adding new scope. I read the pinned sources: HB 136 (2025) §1-1 revises 48-7-29.10(a) to "The amount of such credit shall be equal to 50 percent of the amount of the credit provided for in Section 21 of the Internal Revenue Code", and §3-1(b) makes §1-1 "applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025" — exactly the window the fix installs. I tried amount_mismatch and unrepresented_clause instead, but no encoded number was wrong for the window it was assigned; the defect is a superseded rate left open-ended, which the kind list places under wrong_period_or_effective_date ("timeless encoding of superseded text"), and the fix's pivot is the added effective_to. The one surviving caveat is that the corpus's codified 48-7-29.10 expression (2022-11-01) still reads "Thirty percent for all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2008", so the defect becomes visible only once the 2025 session law is admitted as a source.

Source verification: resolve_provision at rulespec-commit c6db535b07, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current. (a) us-ga/statute/48/48-7-29.10, expression_date 2022-11-01, text "(3) Thirty percent for all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2008." — no terminal date, no 50 percent; the pre-fix proof-atom excerpt matched this verbatim. (b) us-ga/statute/session-laws/2025/hb136/document-1, expression_date 2025-05-13, §1-1 "The amount of such credit shall be equal to 50 percent of the amount of the credit provided for in Section 21 of the Internal Revenue Code", §3-1(b) "Section 1-1 of this Act shall be applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025." Both resolutions reported fix_time_corpus_match = provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref. Reviewer decision point: the pre-fix module's only citation path was the stale codified snapshot, so a strict "wrong against the cited source" reading could downgrade this to not_a_defect (stale corpus, new source admitted by the same campaign — the PR pins the Georgia source chain via rulespec-us #954). I weighed that and rejected it because the unbounded version claimed 2025+ and returned the superseded 0.30 there. PR #907 body supports the repair framing: "repair Georgia PIT law through 2027, including 2026 standard/dependent amounts, the 2027 retirement-income exclusion, the 2025 child-care credit transition". Alternative kinds if a reviewer disagrees: amount_mismatch (2025 rate 0.30 vs 0.50) or unrepresented_clause (the HB 136 amendment clause was absent); both are second-best to the period framing. Also note the module change is co-located with unrelated edits in the same commit (48-7A-3 age-65 logic, 2026 versions on 48-7-26/27), so the commit subject does not describe this module.
